clue.text: Warning remark in preface

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning to people ahead
a word is a brief remark, as in 'a word in your ear'

explanation.surface: A cautionary comment tucked into the opening pages of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an introductory piece at the start of a book is its preface.

clue.text: Unlocked shed found in sort of mine

parts.note: a door that is unlocked can be open
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: An unsecured hut discovered at a mining site.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a mine worked from the surface rather than by shafts is this kind.

clue.text: Just equalised without applause

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the word for equalised wraps round the other piece

parts.note: to equalise is to make level, or even, so equalised is evened
a hand is a round of applause, as in 'give them a big hand'

explanation.surface: A football report: the scores were levelled, but nobody clapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it carries its old meaning of outside, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone just treats all sides fairly and impartially.

clue.text: Hospital visitor

parts.note: suggests a friend dropping in on a ward, but means someone treated at a hospital without staying overnight

explanation.surface: Someone calling at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic sense: a person attending for treatment without being admitted is, literally, a visitor to the hospital.

clue.text: Better, one in a temper

indicators.note: the numeral word is placed in the word for temper

parts.note: dander is temper, as in 'get your dander up'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who is improving, though one of them is in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of dandy in its informal sense of excellent, so finer or better.

clue.text: I had relative in academic stream

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a sister who studied at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isis is the name of the River Thames as it flows through Oxford, hence 'academic stream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the river at Oxford, a university town, is a stream with academic associations.

clue.text: Desire bowled one over in the swimming pool

indicators.note: these two letters are placed in the word for a swimming pool

parts.note: a lido is a public open-air swimming pool
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cricketer bowled someone over beside the pool, prompting some desire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link here, though in cricket it also suggests a set of deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: libido is sexual desire or drive.

clue.text: Central principles taken by economist out of the Good Book

indicators.note: the economist's name takes in, or contains, the abbreviation

parts.note: John Maynard Keynes was a famous British economist
OT, the Old Testament, is a part taken out of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.surface: An economist borrows guiding ideas from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the keynotes of a policy are its central themes or principles.

clue.text: Silly explanation when wife has disappeared in the Orient

indicators.note: the abbreviation for wife vanishes from the word for explanation

parts.note: an answer can be an explanation of something
taken as written
E stands for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A daft account given once a man's wife has gone missing in Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Anserine means goose-like, and so by extension foolish or silly, a goose being proverbially stupid.

clue.text: Be ashamed, creeping along the ground

definitions.meaning: to feel remorse or regret for a wrong
in botany ... (said REE-pent) describes a plant that creeps along the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to feel sorry for sins, and the botanical adjective for a creeping, prostrate plant.

clue.text: Walker is prosaic

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a person travelling on foot, and an adjective for something dull or uninspired.

clue.text: Prince knocking back a glass of beer

indicators.note: drinking slang, read here as turning the phrase backwards

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A royal downing a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a raja is an Indian prince or king.

clue.text: Hide fish out of river initially in waterproof cover

indicators.note: the first letter of river goes in the name of the fish

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of river

parts.note: an animal's hide is its coat

explanation.surface: An angler's skin-and-fish gear, pulled from the river, offers waterproof protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a trenchcoat is a belted waterproof raincoat.

clue.text: Eton's a rich organisation for such an outlet

indicators.note: the letters are organised, or arranged, into a new order

parts.note: the letters of the word, possessive s included
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eton is rich enough to run its own shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such an outlet' points back to the clue: the answer is a shop belonging to a large organisation, which is what the letters make.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a chain store is a retail outlet that is one of many owned by one company.

clue.text: Prude's act I made up for slapstick comedy

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters of the word, the s included
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prim person's routine, invented for a comic sketch.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pie in the face is a classic piece of slapstick comedy.

clue.text: Tried to learn to be deliberate

definitions.meaning: past tense of study, to apply oneself to learning
... as an adjective, carefully planned or intentional

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: having applied oneself to learning, and an adjective for something done intentionally.

clue.text: Glasgow, for example, promoting heroic tale showing wisdom

indicators.note: promoting puts the tale ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a saga is a long heroic story, originally Norse
Glasgow is a city in Scotland

explanation.surface: A Glaswegian epic story that displays great wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'promoting' means moving up, which here puts the tale before the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sagacity is shrewd judgement or wisdom.

clue.text: Ropes in girls to hold the ring

indicators.note: the word for girls holds the ring shape inside it

parts.note: lasses are girls, especially in Scotland and northern England
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Girls in a boxing ring being roped in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lasso is to catch with a rope, so lassoes is ropes in.

clue.text: Given lens, point to the old part

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
ye is an old form of the
a piece is a part

explanation.surface: Someone given a lens and told to point at an antique component.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an eyepiece is the lens at the end of a microscope or telescope nearest the eye.

clue.text: A yob -— ten, perhaps -—— displaying a blade

indicators.note: signals the letters might be rearranged into another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten young thugs flashing knives.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a bayonet is a blade fixed to the muzzle of a rifle.

clue.text: Agreeable music in conveyance without passengers

parts.note: something agreeable is good
a strain is a passage of music or a tune

explanation.surface: Pleasant tunes played on a ride with nobody aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a goods train carries freight, not passengers.

clue.text: Subterfuge getting rid of employee works

indicators.note: the word for employee is removed from the word for subterfuge

parts.note: a manoeuvre is a crafty move or stratagem
a man is a worker, as in 'management and men'

explanation.surface: An underhand scheme to fire staff at the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an oeuvre is the whole body of an artist's works.

clue.text: Old artist, almost backward

indicators.note: the trimmed name is read in reverse
the last letter of the artist's name is dropped

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly painter who is nearly behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts DEGAS to DEGA, and 'backward' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone aged is old.

clue.text: Bouncer bringing stated period of play to an end

indicators.note: the polo term is said aloud to give a word of the same sound

parts.note: a chukker is a period of play in polo
out means finished, at an end

explanation.surface: A doorman bringing a match to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: A chukka or chukker is one of the timed periods in a polo match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a bouncer is a doorman who ejects troublemakers from a club.

clue.text: Ruler had old poem sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rime is an old spelling of rhyme, a poem, as in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: A monarch whose old verses were mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an emir is a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Raptor's very large victim

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large
prey is the victim of a hunter

explanation.surface: A bird of prey's huge quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, a raptor.

clue.text: Sort of road that has to go round top of hill

parts.note: to turn is to rotate or go round
a pike is a peaked hilltop, especially in the Lake District, as in Scafell Pike

explanation.surface: A road that must curve around a hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a turnpike is a toll road, historically barred by a pike-like gate.

clue.text: Losing watts, loudspeaker notes wobbled

indicators.note: the loudspeaker word loses the abbreviation for watts

parts.note: a tweeter is a small loudspeaker for high notes
W is the symbol for watts
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A speaker losing power makes its notes waver.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to teeter is to wobble or sway unsteadily.
